messages:
Nina: quick heads-up, after the midnight rollout i saw short-p99 regress on a couple g5 instances. small interactive calls (<=32 tokens) are hitting ~120ms p99 vs ~85ms baseline.
Chris: saw same in traces. queueing time to first dispatch up by ~20ms when theres a long 1024+ token batch accumulating.
Pavel: i dug into the batcher logs. we now wait up to 7ms to form mixed batches and that seems to favor long sequences getting grouped first.
Isabel: KV stats show modest increase in eviction churn during the same window. short tenants see a KV miss burst coincident with long-batch execution.
Tony: kernel note: the selector chooses high-throughput GEMM path for long requests which pins many SMs and delays small-kernel launches briefly.
Nina: so combo of longer accumulation + kernel occupancy + KV churn. any quick mitigations we can A/B?
Chris: idea: introduce a dedicated short-lane with a small token bank that short requests can drain from immediately. keep it shared but enforce per-tenant fraction to avoid abuse.
Pavel: alternative/additive: reduce mixed-batch max_wait_ms to 4ms for hosts with >30% short-QPS. adaptive threshold.
Isabel: for KV, what about a soft pin: mark recently-accessed keys from short-lane with a short protection window (e.g., 150ms) in eviction metadata so long-run warming doesn't evict them. cheap and ephemeral.
Tony: kernel scheduler change: when short-lane backlog > 10, bias kernel choice toward low-occupancy variants for next N micro-batches so they launch faster. cheap heuristic.
Nina: sounds promising. we should simulate impact on long throughput; acceptable drop might be <=3% for much better p99 for interactive tenants.
Chris: ran a toy sim: short-p99 improved ~35% with short-bank=512 tokens global, per-tenant cap 128. long throughput hit ~1.7%. KV pin cut eviction spikes by ~60%.
Pavel: couple implementation details:
```
- batcher: add config short_bank_base and per_tenant_cap_pct
- reserve sizing: adaptive EWMA: reserve = max(min_base, alpha * short_token_rate)
- kv: kv_protect(tenant, keys[], ttl_ms=150) -> metadata only
- kernel: scheduler_hint('prefer_low_occupancy', duration_ms=100)
```
Isabel: telemetry reqs: add labels queue_blocker=(accum_wait|kernel_busy|kv_eviction|reserve_depleted) and metric short_bank_allocated, short_bank_used, per_tenant_bank_usage.
Tony: logging: emit a sparse trace event when tenant hits cap to find hot tenants hitting per-tenant cap.
Nina: rollout plan? small PR for batcher + telemetry, kernel hint in separate PR. canary on 5 hosts with mixed replay for 2 hours. abort if short-p99 > 150ms or kv_evictions > 3x baseline.
Chris: agree. PR owners: Chris -> batcher + adaptive reserve (today), Pavel -> KV protect + e2e (1d), Tony -> kernel hint (1d), Isabel -> telemetry + dashboards (tomorrow).
Pavel: one nuance: per-tenant cap should be enforced as a soft quota with graceful degradation: once cap hit, short requests can fallback to standard queue with backoff rather than hard drop.
Isabel: tests: 1) even mix 50/50 long-short, 2) skewed 90% long, 3) many small tenants to verify cap fairness. add regression threshold checks.
Chris: also add experiment tag `exp=shortbank_jun2024` to emitted metrics.
ops-bot: canary deployment initiated for eng-runtime-shortbank at 2024-06-18T03:00:00Z :rocket:
Nina: nice. monitoring thresholds set. ill watch the dashboard and collect trace samples during canary. ping if any p99 > 180ms or sustained kv_eviction spike.
Tony: one more thought: adaptive reserve bounds should scale down on memory pressure to avoid worsening KV churn. tie reserve scaling to a KV_eviction_rate signal.
Pavel: good call. add reserve_decay_on_kv_pressure = true.
Isabel: ok i'll add those signals to the telemetry patch so we can observe interactions.
Chris: timeline recap in thread: batcher PR -> today, telemetry -> tomorrow, kv pin -> +1d, kernel hint -> +1d, canary -> Friday.
Nina: thanks team. small iterative changes and solid telemetry will tell us if this protects short tenants without regressing long-run metrics.
